about: The RV32E instructions Tiqora decodes, one example of each kind. Written by hand; every row is assembled by a real assembler (docs/tools/views_isa.py), and its opcode (bits 6:0) is checked against the constant the core's decoder uses. Each row links to the line of tp_ncore that decodes it.

rows.note: load a 20-bit constant into the top of a register
PC-relative address: adds a 20-bit constant, shifted up, to this instruction's address
call: jump, keeping the return address in ra
compare two registers and branch in one instruction; RISC-V has no flags
add a 12-bit constant; no flags are set
three operands: two sources and a separate destination
set a0 to 1 if a1 < a2 (signed), else 0
call the environment; on Tiqora it halts the core
Xpulse TWAIT a0: sleep until the timebase reaches a0 (Tiqora's own custom-0 opcode)
Xpulse TARM a0, a1: arm trigger a1 to fire at time a0, in hardware
